articles.title: राष्ट्रिय इन्जिनियर दिवस घोषणा गर्न इन्जिनियर्स एसोसियसनको माग
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपाल इन्जिनियर्स एसोसियसनका अध्यक्ष सुवासचन्द्र बरालले प्रत्येक वर्ष साउन ३ गते मनाइने इन्जिनियर दिवसलाई सरकारले औपचारिक रूपमा ‘राष्ट्रिय इन्जिनियर दिवस’ घोषणा गरी सरकारी क्यालेन्डरमा समावेश गर्न आग्रह गरेका छन्।

एसोसियसनको ६४औँ इन्जिनियर दिवस समारोहलाई सम्बोधन गर्दै अध्यक्ष बरालले पूर्वाधार र प्रविधि कुनै पनि राष्ट्रको आर्थिक विकास र समृद्धिको मेरुदण्ड भएको उल्लेख गर्दै इन्जिनियरिङ क्षेत्रलाई प्राथमिकतामा राखेर राज्यले दीर्घकालीन नीति अवलम्बन गर्नुपर्ने बताए।

उनका अनुसार नेपालमा दर्ता भएका करिब एक लाख इन्जिनियरमध्ये करिब ६० प्रतिशत युवा छन्। तर पर्याप्त रोजगारी र अवसरको अभावका कारण ठूलो संख्यामा दक्ष जनशक्ति विदेश पलायन भइरहेको भन्दै उनले यसलाई रोक्न तत्काल प्रभावकारी नीति आवश्यक रहेको बताए।

‘युवा इन्जिनियरहरूको सीप, ज्ञान र दक्षताको उचित उपयोग गर्न राज्य, उद्योग र इन्जिनियरिङ समुदायबीच बलियो सहकार्य आवश्यक छ,’ उनले भने।

बरालले यस वर्षको इन्जिनियर दिवस 'Young Mind and Engineering: Shaping Better Nepal' भन्ने मूल नारासहित मनाइएको जानकारी दिँदै विकास निर्माणमा संलग्न प्राविधिकहरूले कार्यस्थलमा असुरक्षा, प्रशासनिक झन्झट र अनावश्यक दबाब झेल्नुपरेको गुनासो गरे। यस्तो अवस्थाले विकास आयोजनाको गति नै प्रभावित भएको उनको भनाइ थियो।

उनले प्राविधिकहरूको क्षमताको अधिकतम उपयोग गर्न पुरस्कार र दण्डको स्पष्ट प्रणाली लागू गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यकता औँल्याए। ऊर्जा, जलस्रोत, कृषि, पर्यटन, सूचना प्रविधि, उद्योग तथा मानव संसाधनलगायत सबै क्षेत्रमा इन्जिनियरहरूको भूमिका निर्णायक रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै बदलिँदो प्रविधिअनुसार सीप विकासमा लगानी बढाउनुपर्नेमा जोड दिए।

सरकारसमक्ष एसोसियसनले इन्जिनियरिङ क्षेत्रसँग सम्बन्धित विभिन्न नीतिगत माग पनि अघि सारेको छ।

अध्यक्ष बरालले विकास निर्माणमा खटिने इन्जिनियरका लागि सुरक्षित कार्य वातावरणको कानुनी प्रत्याभूति, रणनीतिक सरकारी निकायको नेतृत्व तहमा प्राविधिक पृष्ठभूमिका इन्जिनियरहरूको प्रतिनिधित्व, छुट्टै इन्जिनियरिङ सेवा आयोग गठन तथा नेपाल इन्जिनियरिङ प्रशिक्षण तथा अनुसन्धान प्रतिष्ठान स्थापना प्रक्रिया तत्काल अघि बढाउन आग्रह गरे।

त्यसैगरी, युवा इन्जिनियरका लागि पर्याप्त रोजगारी सिर्जना, विकास आयोजनाको सुपरभिजन इन्जिनियरबाटै गराउने व्यवस्था, निजी तथा गैरसरकारी क्षेत्रमा कार्यरत इन्जिनियरहरूको न्यूनतम मासिक पारिश्रमिक ३७ हजार १३५ कार्यान्वयन तथा प्राविधिक त्रुटिलाई स्वतः भ्रष्टाचारको कसुर अन्तर्गत नराख्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था गर्न पनि उनले सरकारसँग माग गरे।

अध्यक्ष बरालले नेपाल इन्जिनियर्स एसोसियसन इन्जिनियरहरूको पेशागत हकहितको संरक्षण, नवप्रवर्तनको प्रवर्द्धन र राज्यसँग इन्जिनियरिङ समुदायलाई जोड्ने साझा संस्थाका रूपमा निरन्तर सक्रिय रहने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गर्दै सम्पूर्ण इन्जिनियर तथा आर्किटेक्टलाई पेशागत नैतिकता र इमान्दारितालाई सर्वोच्च प्राथमिकतामा राखेर समृद्ध नेपाल निर्माणमा योगदान दिन आह्वान गरे।

articles.title: जेनजी आन्दोलन प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनमा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय दबाब
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । गत वर्षको भदौ २३ र २४ गते देशमा भएको जेनजी विद्रोह र त्यसक्रममा भएका गम्भीर मानवअधिकार उल्लंघनका घटनासम्बन्धी राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगको प्रतिवेदन संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघ पुगेको छ ।

नेपालभित्र प्रतिवेदन सार्वजनिक गर्न चौतर्फी माग भइरहेका बेला आयोगले करिब १० हजार पृष्ठ लामो उक्त प्रतिवेदन जेनेभास्थित मानवअधिकार उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयमा पेश गरेको छ।

तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री केपी शर्मा ओली र गृहमन्त्री रमेश लेखकसहित उच्च अधिकारीहरूमाथि फौजदारी अनुसन्धानको सिफारिस गरिएको यो प्रतिवेदन अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मञ्चमा पुगेसँगै अब सरकारमाथि कूटनीतिक र अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय दबाब बढ्ने देखिएको छ ।

गएको भदौ २३–२४ गतेको जेनजी विद्रोहसम्बन्धी राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगको प्रतिवेदन संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघीय मानव अधिकार उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालय ओएचसीएचआर जेनेभामा पेश भएको छ ।

यो प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनका लागि अब सरकारलाई थप दबाब पर्नेछ । जुन १५ देखि जुलाइ ७ सम्म जेनेभामा चलेको ह्युमन राइट काउन्सिलको २४औँ बैठक र ६२ औँ सत्रमा राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगका सदस्य मिहिर ठाकुरले नेपालमा भएको जेनजी विद्रोहको मानवअधिकार अवस्थाका विस्तृत विवरणसहितको प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनका लागि सरकारलाई बुझाएको जानकारी दिँदै सरकारले प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वय गर्नैपर्ने जानकारी गराएका थिए ।

उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयले राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगले पेश गरेको प्रतिवेदनलाई नोटमा राखेको छ । सरकारलाई मानवअधिकार आयोगको प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनका लागि अरु दबाब पर्नेछ । जेनेभा बैठकमा भाग लिन आयोगका सदस्य ठाकुरसँगै आयोगकी उपसचिव माया शर्मा पनि पुगेकी थिइन ।

सरकारमाथि अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय दबाब बढाउने रणनीति

आयोगभित्रैका केही अधिकारीहरूका अनुसार सरकारले प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयन नगर्ने आशंका बढेपछि आयोगले प्रतिवेदन अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मञ्चमा पठाएको हो ।

नेपालमै प्रतिवेदन पूर्णरूपमा सार्वजनिक गर्न आग्रह मानव अधिकार आयोगले आग्रह गरे पनि त्यो सम्भव नभएको बताउने गरेकाले पनि अब जेनेभाबाटै थप प्रक्रिया अगाडि बढ्न सक्ने अवस्था बनेको छ ।

प्रतिवेदनमा को–कोमाथि अनुसन्धान सिफारिस ?

जेनजी आन्दोलनमा भएको दमन, गोली प्रहार, सार्वजनिक सम्पत्तिमा आगजनी तथा विध्वंसका घटनाबारे आयेगको प्रतिवेदन करिब १० हजार पृष्ठको छ । तर आयोगले प्रतिवेदनको केही अंश मात्रै सार्वजनिक गरेको थियो ।

उक्त प्रतिवेदनमा तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री केपी शर्मा ओली, तत्कालीन गृहमन्त्री रमेश लेखक, तत्कालीन सञ्चारमन्त्री पृथ्वी सुब्बा गुरुङ, तत्कालीन प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक चन्द्रकुवेर खापुङ लगायतमाथि फौजदारी अनुसन्धान अघि बढाउन सिफारिस गरिएको छ ।

यसैगरी आन्दोलनका क्रममा भएको विध्वंसमा कलाकार, पत्रकार, इन्फ्लुएन्सर तथा हाल संसद् र सरकारमा रहेका केही व्यक्तिहरूमाथि पनि थप अनुसन्धान गर्न आयोगले सिफारिस गरेको छ ।

आन्दोलनका घटनाबारे आयोगको निष्कर्ष

पूर्ण प्रतिवेदनमा भदौ २३ देखि २६ सम्मका घटना समेटिएका छन् । कसले कोसँग संवाद ग¥यो ?के–के कुरा भयो ? सार्वजनिक सम्पत्तिमा आगो लगाउनेसम्ममा कसको योजना थियो भन्ने समेटिएका छन् ।

भीड कसरी उग्र बन्यो, सार्वजनिक सम्पत्तिमा आगजनी गर्ने योजना कसरी बनेको थियो भन्ने विवरण पनि प्रतिवेदनमा समावेश छ । आयोगले अनुसन्धानका लागि आवश्यक केही प्रमाण, विशेषगरी गोलीका अवशेष बुलेट संकलन गर्न नसकिएको स्वीकार गरेको छ ।

ओली–लेखकले नै मागेका छन्, प्रतिवेदनको प्रतिलिपि

आयोगको पूर्ण प्रतिवेदन सार्वजनिक गर्न माग भइरहँदा फौजदारी अनुसन्धान अघि बढाउन सिफारिस गरिएका पूर्व प्रधानमन्त्री एवम् एमाले अध्यक्ष ओली, पूर्व गृहमन्त्री एवम् कांग्रेस नेता रमेश लेखक, पूर्व सञ्चार मन्त्री पृथ्वी सुब्बा गुरुङले प्रतिवेदनमाथि प्रश्न उठाउँदै आयोगसमक्ष निवेदन दर्ता गराएका छन् ।

प्रतिवेदनको केही अंश झिकिएको र केही अंश थपिएको आशंकापछि उनीहरुले प्रतिवेदन माग गरेका हुन् । ओलीको तर्फबाट छानबिन तथा अनुसन्धान प्रतिवेदन माग गर्दै एमाले नेता महेश बर्तौलाले असार १२ गते आयोगमा निवेदन दर्ता गराएका थिए ।

ओलीले आयोगको बैठकको निर्णय नम्बर १७७ को प्रमाणित प्रतिलिपि, लिली थापा नेतृत्वको समितिले आयोगमा पेश गरेको प्रतिवेदनको प्रतिलिपि, प्रतिवेदनमा थपघट गरिएको अंश र थपघट गर्नुको कारणसमेत माग गरेका छन् ।

यस्तै, रास्वपा सभापति रवि लामिछानेलाई कारागारबाट बाहिर निकाल्न गएको आरोप लागेका सांसद दीपक बोहोराले पनि आयोगमा निवेदन दिएका थिए । आयोगले भनेको समयमा आफू अस्पतालमा रहेको उनको दलिल छ ।

उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयमा प्रतिवेदन पेश भएपछि के हुन्छ ?

संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघको मानवअधिकार उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयले अब चार चरणमा प्रक्रिया अघि बढाउँछ ।

पहिलो चरण : अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय अभिलेखः–

प्रतिवेदन संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघको आधिकारिक अभिलेखमा दर्ता हुन्छ । यसले नेपालमा मानव अधिकार उल्लंघन भएको दाबी अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय निगरानीमा प्रवेश गर्छ ।

दोस्रो चरण : प्रश्न र स्पष्टीकरणः–

मानव अधिकार परिषद्का सदस्य राष्ट्रहरूले नेपाल सरकारसँग स्पष्टीकरण माग्न सक्छन् ।

तेस्रो चरण : सिफारिसः–

उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालय वा विशेष प्रतिवेदकहरूले नेपाललाई अनुसन्धान, पीडितलाई क्षतिपूर्ति वा जिम्मेवार व्यक्तिमाथि कारबाही गर्न सिफारिस गर्न सक्छन् ।

चौथो चरण : निगरानीः–

नेपालले ती सिफारिस कार्यान्वयन ग¥यो कि गरेन भनेर आगामी सत्रहरूमा पुनःसमीक्षा हुन्छ ।

जेनजी प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनमा दबाब

जेनजी आन्दोलनको प्रतिवेदन अब नेपालको आन्तरिक राजनीतिक विवाद मात्र रहेन, अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मानव अधिकार बहसको विषय बनेको छ । मानव अधिकार परिषद्को ६२औँ सत्रमा यसबारे औपचारिक जानकारी प्रस्तुत भइसकेकाले नेपाल सरकारले प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयन नगरेमा आगामी सत्रहरूमा थप प्रश्न उठ्न सक्छन् ।

यद्यपी प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयन नगरेकै कारण कुनै देशलाई तुरुन्त प्रतिबन्ध भने लाग्दैन ।तर अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय आलोचना बढ्छ । मानव अधिकार सम्बन्धी वार्षिक प्रतिवेदनमा नकारात्मक उल्लेख हुन्छ । यसको असरले वैदेशिक सहायता र विकास साझेदारहरूको दबाब बढ्न सक्छ ।

त्यस्तै, विशेष प्रतिवेदक वा अनुसन्धान टोली पठाउने सम्भावना पनि रहन्छ। नेपालमा विगतमा द्वन्द्वकालीन मानव अधिकार उल्लंघनका विषयमा संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघले पटक–पटक चासो व्यक्त गरेको छ ।

यस्ता घटनामा कुन कुन देशलाई प्रतिबन्ध लागेको छ ?

मानव अधिकार उल्लंघनका आधारमा विभिन्न देशहरूमा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको उदाहरणहरु छन् । म्यानमारमा सैन्य दमन र मानव अधिकार उल्लंघनको घटनामा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको छ भने इरानमा प्रदर्शनकारीमाथि दमन गरेको भन्दै मानवअधिकार उल्लंघन भएको निश्कर्षमा प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको छ।

त्यस्तै मानवअधिकार उल्लंघनका घटना छानबिन गरेर कारवाही नगरेका कारण बेलारुस, गृहयुद्ध र मानवअधिकार उल्लंघनका कारण सिरिया लगायतका देश प्रतिबन्धमा परेका छन् ।

articles.title: झापाका ४२ परिवार तनावमा, अन्तिम किस्ता रोकिएपछि छटपटि
articles.summary:
झापा । झापाको मेचीनगरस्थित दिपज्योती टोलका ४२ परिवार दुई दशकअघि किस्ताबन्दीमा खरिद गरेको जग्गाको लालपूर्जा नपाउँदा समस्यामा परेका छन् । मेचीनगर २ र ३ को सिमानास्थित जग्गा हालसम्म नामसारी हुन नसक्दा पीडित परिवारको समस्या झन् जटिल बन्दै गएको छ ।

झापाको मेचीनगर ३ स्थित बजगाई टि–स्टेट प्रालिको नाममा रहेको चिया बगान नभएको खाली जग्गा वि.स २०६३÷०६४ सालमा शुभ चिया प्रालिले बैना गरि घरघडेरीका लागि स्थानीयलाई किस्ताबन्दी एकदेखि पाँच कठ्ठासम्म बिक्री प्रक्रिया अगाडी बढायो ।

सुकुम्बासी तथा न्यून आय भएका परिवारलाई लक्षित गरी बिक्री गरिएको उक्त जग्गाको अधिकांश किस्ता तिरे पनि अन्तिम किस्ता लिएपछि लालपूर्जा उपलब्ध गराउने सहमति कार्यान्वयन नभएको पीडितहरूको भनाइ छ ।

अन्तिम किस्ता पनि तिर्न तयार भएका उनीहरुको संस्थाले रकम नै लिएन । अहिले उनीहरुको न पैसा फिर्ता भएको छ, न लालपूर्जा नै पाएका छन् ।

त्यस्तै पीडित स्थानीयका अनुसार जग्गा बजगाई टि–स्टेट प्रालिको नाममा रहे पनि तत्कालीन शुभ चिया प्रालिका अध्यक्ष हेमराज भारतीले कारोबार अगाडी बढाएका थिए । तर उनले पैसा लिएपछि त्यसलाई कार्यान्वयन गर्न आलटाल गरेको दुखेसो पीडित पोख्छन् । उनीहरुले जग्गा समस्या तत्काल समाधानका लागि सम्बन्धित निकायसँग माग गरेका छन्।

यता शुभ चिया प्रालिका वर्तमान अध्यक्ष रमेश दाहालले विगतमा कारोबार संस्थागत प्रक्रियाअनुसार नभएकाले समस्या उत्पन्न भएको बताउँछन् । समस्या समाधानका लागि सम्बन्धित सरोकारवाला निकायसँग आवश्यक गृहकार्य भइरहेको र पीडितलाई न्याय दिलाउने प्रयास जारी रहेको उनको भनाइ छ ।

सुकुम्बासी तथा न्यून आय भएका परिवारले साहुसंग ऋण गरेर किस्ता वापतको रकम समेत दिइ सकेको अवस्थामा अन्तिम किस्ता नलिई जग्गाको स्वामित्व समेत प्रदान नगर्दा ४२ परिवार समस्यामा परेका छन् । तसर्थ उनीहरुलाई सम्बन्धित सरोकारवाला निकायले यथाशिघ्र समस्या समाधान गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यक देखिन्छ ।

articles.title: नेपाल लाइफको ऐतिहासिक कीर्तिमान, १३ अर्बभन्दा बढी प्रथम बीमा आर्जन
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालको सर्वाधिक विश्वासिलो जीवन बीमा कम्पनीका रूपमा स्थापित नेपाल लाइफ इन्स्योरेन्सले आफ्नो २५ वर्षको गौरवमय यात्रा (सिल्भर जुबिली) का अवसरमा रु. १३ अर्बभन्दा बढी प्रथम बीमा शुल्क (FPI) आर्जन गर्दै जीवन बीमा इतिहासमा नयाँ ऐतिहासिक कीर्तिमान कायम गरेको छ।

गत आर्थिक वर्षमा रु. १० अर्ब प्रथम बीमा शुल्क आर्जन गरेको कम्पनीले यस वर्ष उक्त उपलब्धिलाई अझ उचाइमा पुर्‍याउँदै बीमा उद्योगमा नयाँ मानक स्थापित गरेको हो।

यस ऐतिहासिक सफलताका अवसरमा कम्पनीका प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत प्रवीण रमण पराजुलीले सम्पूर्ण बीमित, अभिकर्ता, कर्मचारी, शेयरधनी तथा सरोकारवालाहरू प्रति आभार व्यक्त गर्दै आगामी दिनमा अझ थप प्रविधिमैत्री सेवा, नवीन बीमा योजना र उत्कृष्ट सेवा प्रदान गर्ने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरे ।

articles.title: सिद्धार्थ बैंकद्वारा ‘सिद्धार्थ गोल्ड लोन’ सुविधा सञ्चालनमा
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । सिद्धार्थ बैंक लिमिटेडले ग्राहकहरुको तत्कालको वित्तीय आवश्यकतालाई सहज र सर्वसुलभ बनाउने उद्देश्यका साथ नयाँ कर्जा योजना ‘सिद्धार्थ गोल्ड लोन’ सार्वजनिक गरेको छ।

यस योजना अन्तर्गत ग्राहकहरुले आफ्नो सुन तथा सुनका गरगहनाहरु धितो राखी बैंकबाट अधिकतम रु. ५० लाखसम्मको कर्जा रकम प्राप्त गर्न सक्नेछन्, जसमा धितो सुनको मूल्यांकनका आधारमा बढीमा ७५ प्रतिशतसम्म कर्जा प्रवाह गरिनेछ।

ग्राहकहरूले आफ्नो व्यक्तिगत तथा व्यावसायिक आवश्यकता सहज रूपमा पूरा गर्न सकुन् भन्ने उद्देश्यले सञ्चालनमा ल्याइएको यो सुरक्षित र भरपर्दो सुविधा हालका लागि बैंकको काठमाडौंस्थित न्यूरोड गेट शाखाबाट उपलब्ध छ, र यस सम्बन्धी थप जानकारीका लागि बैंकको २४ सै घण्टा सञ्चालनमा रहने ग्राहक सेवा केन्द्र ‘सिद्धार्थ केयर’ मा सम्पर्क गर्न सकिनेछ।

articles.title: कतारमा नेपाली समुदायद्वारा स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरप्रति श्रद्धाञ्जली
articles.summary:
कतार । गैरआवासीय नेपाली संघ (एनआरएनए) राष्ट्रिय समन्वय परिषद् (एनसीसी) कतारले स्वर्गीय हिज हाइनेस फादर अमिर शेख हमद बिन खलिफा अल थानीप्रति श्रद्धाञ्जली अर्पण गर्न शोकसभा आयोजना गरेको छ।

कार्यक्रममा उनको दूरदर्शी नेतृत्व तथा कतारको समृद्धि, विकास र विश्वमञ्चमा स्थापित गराउन पुर्‍याएको अतुलनीय योगदानको उच्च सम्मान गरिएको थियो।

कार्यक्रममा कतारस्थित नेपाली राजदूतावासका कूटनीतिज्ञ प्रेमप्रसाद पोखरेल प्रमुख अतिथिका रूपमा सहभागी भएका थिए। साथै कतारमा क्रियाशील विभिन्न नेपाली सामाजिक तथा कल्याणकारी संस्थाका प्रतिनिधिहरूको उल्लेखनीय उपस्थिति रहेको थियो। शोकको यस घडीमा नेपाली समुदायले एकता र ऐक्यबद्धता प्रदर्शन गरेको आयोजकले जनाएको छ।

कार्यक्रमको सुरुआत पवित्र कुरआनको तिलावतबाट भएको थियो भने मौलाना गुलाम नबी रजबीले स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरको आत्माको चिरशान्तिको कामना गर्दै कतार राज्यको शान्ति, स्थायित्व र समृद्धिका लागि विशेष दुआ गरेका थिए।

एनआरएनए एनसीसी कतारका अध्यक्ष कृष्ण पन्थीले स्वागत मन्तव्य दिँदै स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरको निधनप्रति गहिरो दुःख व्यक्त गरे।

उनले कतारका अमिर, राजपरिवार, सरकार तथा सम्पूर्ण कतारी जनताप्रति समवेदना व्यक्त गर्दै स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरको दूरदर्शी नेतृत्व, राष्ट्र निर्माणमा खेलेको ऐतिहासिक भूमिका र उनले छोडेको प्रेरणादायी विरासतको प्रशंसा गरे। पन्थीले कतारलाई विश्वकै सम्मानित र समृद्ध राष्ट्रका रूपमा स्थापित गर्न फादर अमिरको योगदान अविस्मरणीय रहेको बताए।

कार्यक्रमका प्रमुख वक्ता प्राध्यापक मोहम्मद रमजान अली मियाँले नेपाल–कतारबीचको लामो समयदेखिको मित्रवत सम्बन्ध र बढ्दो सहकार्यबारे चर्चा गरे। उनले स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरको नेतृत्वमा कतारले आर्थिक विविधीकरण, शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य, पूर्वाधार विकास तथा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय कूटनीतिमा उल्लेखनीय प्रगति हासिल गरेको बताए। साथै कतारले हजारौँ नेपालीलाई रोजगारी तथा अवसर उपलब्ध गराउँदै आएको उल्लेख गर्दै त्यसप्रति आभार व्यक्त गरे।

कतारस्थित नेपाली दूतावासका तर्फबाट बोल्दै कूटनीतिज्ञ प्रेमप्रसाद पोखरेलले स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरप्रति श्रद्धाञ्जली अर्पण गर्दै उनको योगदानको उच्च प्रशंसा गरे।

उनले नेपाल–कतारबीचको मैत्रीपूर्ण सम्बन्ध निरन्तर सुदृढ हुँदै आएको उल्लेख गर्दै आगामी दिनमा दुई देशबीचको सहयोग र मित्रतालाई अझ मजबुत बनाउने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरे।

कार्यक्रममा सहभागी विभिन्न नेपाली संघ–संस्थाका प्रतिनिधिहरूले पनि शोक मन्तव्य व्यक्त गर्दै कतारले नेपाली समुदायलाई प्रदान गरेको अवसरप्रति आभार प्रकट गरे। साथै कठिन घडीमा कतारका नेतृत्व र जनताप्रति ऐक्यबद्धता तथा सम्मान व्यक्त गरे।

श्रद्धाञ्जली सभा अन्त्यमा स्वर्गीय हिज हाइनेस शेख हमद बिन खलिफा अल थानीको सम्मानमा सामूहिक प्रार्थना तथा एक मिनेट मौनधारण गरिएको थियो। कार्यक्रममा वक्ताहरूले उनको दूरदर्शी नेतृत्व र योगदानले आगामी पुस्तालाई पनि प्रेरणा दिइरहने विश्वास व्यक्त गरेका थिए।

articles.title: मिटर ब्याज पीडितलाई मनाउन सुधनको कसरत, बल्ल माने पीडित
articles.summary:
बारा । बाराको निजगढ नगरपालिका–८ स्थित निजगढ नगर उद्योग वाणिज्य संघको सभाहलमा तीन दिनदेखि जारी सरकार र मिटरब्याजविरुद्ध किसान–मजदुर आन्दोलनको निर्णायक वार्ता अब राजधानी काठमाडौंमा हुने भएको छ । मिटरब्याज पीडित सरकारसँग वार्ता गर्न जहाजबाट काठमाडौं आएका छन् ।

जनकपुरबाट काठमाडौंतर्फ पैदल न्याय मार्चमा रहेका मिटरब्याजविरुद्ध किसान–मजदुर आन्दोलन, नेपालका प्रतिनिधिहरूसँग गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङले बुधबार करिब पाँच घण्टा लामो छलफल गरेका थिए । छलफलका क्रममा आन्दोलनकारीहरूले उठाएका छ बुँदे मागबारे विस्तृत रूपमा कुराकानी भएको थियो ।

आन्दोलन पक्षका अनुसार सरकारले उनीहरूले अघि सारेका सम्पूर्ण माग कार्यान्वयन गर्ने प्रतिबद्धता जनाएको छ । बुधबार राति निष्कर्षविहीन बनेको वार्तापछि नेपाल सरकारका गृहमन्त्री सुदन गुरुङले आन्दोलनकारीलाई वार्ता टोली गठन गरी सिंहदरबारस्थित गृह मन्त्रालयमा आउन आग्रह गरेका थिए ।

वार्ताका क्रममा गृहमन्त्री गुरुङले सहमतिपत्रमा रहेका केही शब्द तथा भाषागत विषयमा संशोधन गर्न आवश्यक रहेको बताएका थिए । कानुनी तथा प्राविधिक पक्षसमेत मिलाउनुपर्ने भएकाले तत्काल हस्ताक्षर गर्नु उपयुक्त नहुने उनको भनाइ थियो ।

त्यसपछि गृहमन्त्रीको पटक–पटकको आग्रह र आन्दोलनकारी पक्षको आन्तरिक छलफलपछि मिटरब्याजविरुद्ध किसान–मजदुर आन्दोलन, नेपालले पाँच सदस्यीय वार्ता टोली गठन गरी बिहीबार काठमाडौं प्रस्थान गरेको हो । अन्य आन्दोलनकारी भने वार्ताको नतिजा नआएसम्म बाराको निजगढमै रहने जनाइएको छ ।

काठमाडौं प्रस्थान आएको पाँच सदस्यीय वार्ता टोलीको संयोजकमा केन्द्रीय अध्यक्ष अवधेश कुश्वाहा रहेका छन् । टोलीमा केन्द्रीय महासचिव मनोज कुमार पासवान, केन्द्रीय प्रवक्ता रिजन राना मगर, केन्द्रीय हेडक्वाटर सदस्य लक्ष्मी घिमिरे तथा केन्द्रीय हेडक्वाटर सदस्य किरण परियार सदस्य रहेका छन् । वार्ता टोलीको रोहबरमा संयुक्त जनअधिकार मोर्चाका केन्द्रीय अध्यक्ष निर्ग नवीन लगायतका प्रतिनिधिहरू पनि काठमाडौं आएका छन् ।

आन्दोलनका केन्द्रीय अध्यक्ष अवधेश कुश्वाहाले सरकारले माग पूरा गर्न सकारात्मक प्रतिबद्धता जनाएको भए पनि त्यसलाई कानुनी रूपमा स्पष्ट र लिखित रूपमा सुनिश्चित गर्नुपर्ने बताए ।

उनले आन्दोलनकारीको उद्देश्य सहमतिपत्रमा हस्ताक्षर मात्र नभई त्यसको प्रभावकारी कार्यान्वयन सुनिश्चित गर्नु रहेको उल््लेख गर्दै वार्ता सकारात्मक निष्कर्षमा पुग्ने विश्वास व्यक्त गरेका छन् ।

articles.title: कांग्रेस नेता अभिषेक गिरीको अपराध साम्राज्य !
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । ‘हिजो गल्ती भयो, अब समाजसेवामा लाग्छु’ भनी करिब तीन वर्षअघि कारागारबाट छुट्दा अभिषेक गिरीले दिएको सन्देशले धेरैलाई उनी बदलिएको विश्वास दिलाएको थियो । तर, समाजसेवाको आवरणमा पुरानै आपराधिक सञ्जाल सञ्चालन गरेको आरोपमा अहिले उनी फेरि प्रहरी नियन्त्रणमा छन् । मोरङ प्रहरी र केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्युरो (सीआईबी) दुवैले उनीविरुद्ध ठगी र आपराधिक विश्वासघातसम्बन्धी उजुरीमाथि अनुसन्धान गरिरहेका छन् ।

२०७९ चैत ५ गते नौ वर्ष जेल सजाय भुक्तान गरेर कारागारबाट निस्कँदा अभिषेक गिरी साधु भएको आभाष दिलाएका थिए । विगतका गल्ती नदोहो¥याउने प्रतिवद्धता जनाउँदै उनले समाजसेवामा समर्पित हुने घोषणा गरेका थिए ।

त्यसपछि उनले ‘गिरी फाउन्डेसन’ स्थापना गरे, सामाजिक कार्यक्रममा सक्रिय देखिए र आर्थिक रूपमा विपन्नलाई सहयोग गर्न थाले । तर, प्रहरी अनुसन्धानले अभिषेक समाजसेवाको आडमा आपराधिक क्रियाकलापमा संलग्न रहेको भन्दै गम्भीर प्रश्न उठाएको छ ।

गिरीमाथि लागेको आरोप के हो ?

अहिले सीआईबीले अनुसन्धानका लागि मोरङबाट काठमाडौं ल्याएका गिरीलाई यसअघि जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय मोरङले पक्राउ गरेको थियो । उनी पक्राउ परेको विषय पनि निकै रोचक छ । कारागार बाहिरका मान्छेको कारागारभित्र कुनै पहुँच हुँदैन ।

कुनै कैदीबन्दीलाई भेट्न जानु प¥यो भने पनि भेटघाटको कारण खुलाउँदै प्रशासनको अनुमति लिएर सुरक्षा जाँच पार गर्नुपर्ने हुन्छ । अझ कारागारभित्रको प्रशासनको बाहिर कुनै साइनो नै हुँदैन । यति सुरक्षित रहने कारागारको शासन भने गिरीले बाहिरै बसेर चलाउँथे ।

कैदीबन्दीको रासन भत्तामा समेत कब्जा जमाएर असुल्ने गरेको भन्दै गिरीविरुद्ध कैदीबन्दीले नै आवाज उठाएका थिए ।

कैदीबन्दीले बनाएको मुढा र गलैँचाको पैसा गिरीले बुझ्ने गरेको आरोप छ । असार १२ गते कैदीबन्दीलाई बाँडेको १३ लाख ४० हजार रुपैयाँ असुल गरेको आरोप पनि गिरीमाथि छ ।

कारागारभित्रको खाद्यान्न र तरकारी आपूर्तिमा समेत उनको सिन्डिकेट चल्ने गरेको कैदीबन्दीको गुनासो थियो । प्रहरीका अनुसार, गिरीमाथि अहिले दुई फरक प्रकृतिका आरोपमा अनुसन्धान भइरहेको छ ।

मोरङमा कारागारभित्र हुने आर्थिक गतिविधिमा बाहिरबाट प्रभाव पार्दै कैदीबन्दीको रासन भत्ता, उनीहरूले उत्पादन गरेका सामग्रीको रकम तथा आपूर्ति व्यवस्थामा अवैध हस्तक्षेप गरेको आरोपका आधारमा असार १३ गते मोरङ प्रहरीले उनलाई पक्राउ गरेको हो । उनको घरमा गरिएको खानतलासीका क्रममा नगद गन्ने मेसिनसमेत फेला परेको प्रहरीले जनाएको छ ।

उच्च अदालत विराटनगरको आदेशपछि उनी मोरङबाट छुटे पनि त्यही दिन सीआईबीले पुनः नियन्त्रणमा लियो । यसपटक भने निर्माण व्यवसायी सुवास श्रेष्ठको उजुरीका आधारमा अनुसन्धान अघि बढाइएको छ ।

पहुँचका आधारमा ठेक्का दिलाइदिने आश्वासन दिएर ठगी गरेको, निर्माण उपकरण नियन्त्रणमा लिएको तथा जबर्जस्ती सम्पत्ति हस्तान्तरण गराएको आरोपमा आपराधिक विश्वासघात र ठगीसम्बन्धी अनुसन्धान भइरहेको सीआईबीको भनाइ छ । प्रहरीले घटनासँग सम्बन्धित प्रमाण संकलन र बयान लिने काम जारी रहेको जनाएको छ ।

अभिषेक गिरीको आपराधिक पृष्ठभूमि

अभिषेक गिरीको आपराधिक पृष्ठभूमि भने लामो छ । प्रहरीको अभिलेखअनुसार उनी पहिलो पटक २०५८ सालमा पक्राउ परेका थिए । त्यसयता कुटपिट, सार्वजनिक अपराध, डाँका चोरी, ज्यान मार्ने उद्योग र अन्ततः अपहरण तथा शरीर बन्धकजस्ता विभिन्न मुद्दामा उनी ११ पटकसम्म पक्राउ परिसकेका छन् ।

२०७१ सालमा अपहरण तथा शरीर बन्धक मुद्दामा दोषी ठहर भएपछि उनले लामो जेल सजाय भुक्तान गरेका थिए । कारागारबाट छुटेपछि उनी सामाजिक र राजनीतिक गतिविधिमा समेत सक्रिय बने । तर, पछिल्ला घटनाक्रमले उनको पुनः आपराधिक गतिविधिसँग सम्बन्ध रहेको आरोपलाई प्रहरीले गम्भीर रूपमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

अनुसन्धान अझै जारी रहेकाले उनीमाथि लागेको आरोप अदालतबाट प्रमाणित भइसकेको अवस्था भने होइन । अब प्रहरी अनुसन्धान र अदालतको अन्तिम निर्णयले अभिषेक गिरीको कर्तुतको नयाँ पर्दाफास हुनेछ ।

articles.title: अपरेसन चार्लीबाट खुलेको रहस्य, नक्कली नोट छाप्ने गिरोह पक्राउ
articles.summary:
रुपन्देही । रुपन्देही प्रहरीले नक्कली नेपाली नोट, नोट छाप्न प्रयोग गरिएका उपकरण र त्यसमा संलग्न मानिसहरुलाई पक्राउ गरी सार्वजनिक गरेको छ । जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय भैरहवामा बुधबार पत्रकार सम्मेलन गरी प्रहरीले उक्त कार्यमा संलग्नहरु बारे जानकारी दिएको हो ।

रुपन्देही प्रहरीले नक्कली नोट, छाप्ने मेसिनरी उपकरणसहित ६ जनालाई पक्राउ गरेको छ । असार २६ गते बुटवलमा चिनजानकै गंगा कुमारी पुर्वछानेले एक महिलालाई इसेवामार्फत् २ हजार १ सय रुपैयाँ ट्रान्सफर गर्न लगाएर दुईवटा हजारका नोट दिएकी थिइन् ।

पछि ती नोट नक्कली भएको थाहा पाएपछि पीडित महिलाले इलाका प्रहरी कार्यालय बुटवलमा निवेदन दिएकी थिइन् । पूर्वछानेलाई नियन्त्रणमा लिएर अनुसन्धान गर्ने क्रममा नक्कली नोट, छाप्ने मेसिनरी उपकरणसहित प्रहरीले ६ जनालाई पक्राउ गरेको हो ।

अनुसन्धानका क्रममा बुटवल र पोखराका आरोपीहरुका घरबाट समेत नक्कली एक हजार दरका नोट प्रहरीले बरामद गरेको छ ।

डीएसपी चन्दका अनुसार पक्राउ पर्नेमा रुपन्देहीको बुटवल

उपमहानगरपालिका–११, सिर्जनानगर बस्ने बर्ष ३६ की गंगा कुमारी पुर्वछाने, कास्कीको पोखरा महानगरपालिका–१ बस्ने कृष्ण भन्ने किरण कृष्ण तिवारी, भक्तपुरको चाँगुनारायण नगरपालिका–१ बस्ने रामचन्द्र खत्री, कपिलवस्तुको बाणगंगा नगरपालालिका–२ बस्ने संजय थारु, दोलखाको सैलुङ गाउँपालिका–४ वस्ने वर्ष ३८ को पासाङ तामाङ र भारत पश्चिम बंगाल सिलुगुढी भक्तिनगर थाना बस्ने वर्ष ४९ को बासुमित्र आनन्द रहेका छन् ।

उनीहरुको घर तथा शरीर खानतलासीको क्रममा तयार भएका सक्कली जस्तो देखिने एक हजार दरका नक्कली नेपाली नोट ६ सय २२ थान बरामद गरिएको डीएसपी चन्दले बताए ।

प्रहरी फोटोकपी मेसिन, डेल कम्पनीको ल्याप्टप, नक्कली नोट कटिङ गर्न प्रयोग हुने मेसिन, नक्कली नोट प्रिन्ट गर्न प्रयोग हुने प्रिन्टर, नक्कली नोट छाप्न प्रयोग गर्ने पेपर १ कार्टुन पनि बरामद गरेको छ ।

यस्तै, नक्कली नोट बनाउन प्रयोग हुने केमिकल, लेमिलेसन मेसिन, प्लाष्टिक पेपर र ६ वटा मोबाइल पनि प्रहरीले बरामद गरेको छ ।

पीडित महिलाको निवेदनका आधारमा लुम्बिनी प्रदेश प्रहरी कार्यालय दाङ, जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय र इलका प्रहरी कार्यालय बुटवलले ‘अपरेसन चार्ली’ नाम दिएर नक्कली नोट सम्बन्धी संयुक्त अनुसन्धान सुरु गरेका थिए ।

पक्राउ गरेमा ६ जनाविरुद्ध रुपन्देही जिल्ला अदालतबाट मुद्रा सम्बन्धी कसूरमा ५ दिनको म्याद थप गरी अनुसन्धान जारी राखिएको प्रहरीे जनाएको छ । रुपन्देहीमा यसअघि पनि लुम्बिनी, सालझण्डी र बुटवलमै नक्कली नोट बरामद भएका थिए ।

articles.title: गृहमन्त्रीको आश्वासनपछि तेस्रो वार्ताको पखाईमा मिटरब्याजपीडित
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । प्रधानमन्त्री एवम् रास्वपा बरिष्ठ नेता बालेन्द्र शाहले न्याय खोज्न कोही पनि काठमाडौं जानु नपर्ने, काठमाडौं घुम्न र पशुपतिको दर्शन गर्न मात्रै जाने अवस्था आउने भनी मधेस प्रदेशमै गएर आश्वासन दिएका थिए ।

रास्वपालाई मधेसबाट जनताले भारी मत दिएर जिताए पनि ।तर प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले भनेजस्तो न्याय नपाएपछि न्याय खोज्न मिटरब्याज पीडितको एक समूहले जनकपुरबाट काठमाडौंका लािग पैदल यात्रा अघि बढायो।

पटक पटकको सहमति कार्यान्वयन नभएपछि आजित भएका उनीहरु निर्णायक आन्दोलन शुरु गरेका हुन् ।यसपाली जनकपुरबाट बाराको निजगढ आइपुग्दा गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङले आश्वासनको पोको फुकाएका छन् ।

न्यायको माग गर्दै जनकपुरबाट असार २५ गते सुरु भएको मिटरब्याज पीडितको पैदलयात्रा मंगलबार छैटौं दिन बाराको निजगढ आइपुग्यो । काठमाडौंतर्फ अघि बढ्दै गरेको उनीहरुको यात्रा भने निजगढमै रोकिएको छ ।

गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङ मंगलबार निजगढ पुगेर उक्त समूहसँग वार्ता गरि माग पूरा गर्ने आश्वास दिएपछि यात्रा रोकिएको हो । गृहमन्त्री गुरुङले पीडितको माग पूरा गर्न ३ दिनको समय मागेपछि उनीहरु निजगढमै रोकिएका हुन् । तर माग पूरा नभए उनीहरुको यात्रा पुनः काठमाडौंतर्फ अघि बढ्नेछ ।

पीडितहरूले तमसुक व्यवस्था खारेज गर्न, मिटरब्याजसम्बन्धी विशेष ऐन ल्याउन, मिटरब्याजका नाममा गुमेको चल–अचल सम्पत्ति फिर्ता गराउन तथा दोषीमाथि कानुनी कारबाही गर्न आफनो सरकारसँग माग गरिरहेका छन् ।

२०७९ सालदेखि निरन्तर राज्यको ढोका ढक्ढकाउँदै आएका पीडितहरुले मिटरब्याज नियन्त्रणका लागि बनेका कानुन, कार्यविधि तथा सरकारसँग भएका सम्झौताहरू प्रभावकारी रूपमा कार्यान्वयन नभएपछि पुनः आन्दोलनको बाटो रोजेका हुन् । यसअघि उनीहरु दुई दुई पटक काठमाडौं आएर सरकारसँग सहमति गरेका थिए ।

मिटरब्याज पीडितको पैदलमार्चको श्रृङ्गखला

पहिलो पैदल मार्च

मिटरब्याज पीडित पहिलो पटक २०७९ चैत २ गते महोत्तरीको बर्दिबासबाट पैदल मार्चपास गर्दै काठमाडौं आएका थिए ।बर्दिबासबाट निस्किएका मधेशका ७२ जना मिटरब्याज पीडित ११ दिनमा काठमाडौं आईपुगेका थिए।आन्दोलन चर्की पछि चैत १८ गते सरकार र आन्दोलनकारी बिच पाँच बुँदे सहमति भयो।त्यस बेला पुष्पकमल दाहाल प्रचण्ड प्रधानमन्त्री थिए।सहमति अनुसार सरकारले विशेष अदालतका पूर्वअध्यक्ष गौरीबहादुर कार्कीको नेतृत्वमा जाँचबुझ आयोग गठन गर्यो।

सो आयोगमा २८ हजार भन्दा बढी उजुरी परे।पिडितको संख्या ठूलो भएपनि आयोगको म्याद सकिदाँ सम्म न्याय भने एकदम कम मात्रले पाए।जसमा १५ हजार उजुरीमाथि छानबिन भए पनि ५ हजार ५०० फस्र्यौट भएको थियो।तर अधिकांशमा भने कुनै सुनुवाई नै भएन।

दोस्रो पैदल मार्च

पहिलो पैदल मार्च भएको एक बर्ष नबित्दै मिटर ब्याज पिडित फेरि काठमाडौंमा लागि निस्किए । २०८० माघ १६ गते मेची र महाकालीबाट एकैपटक मिटरब्याज तथा ठगी बिरुद्ध पिडितहरुको पैदल मार्च निस्कियो । दोस्रो पैदल मार्चमा करिब ४ सयको संख्यामा पिडित सहभागी थिए ।

काठमाडौंमा उनीहरुको सशंक्त आन्दोलनपछि २०८० फागुन २८ गते फेरि सरकार र मिटरब्याज पिडित बिच वार्ता भइ अर्को चार बुँदे सहमति भयो ।

दोस्रो सहमतिपछि २०८० चैत ९ गते सरकारले पुनः पूर्वन्यायाधीश तेजबहादुर कार्कीको नेतृत्वमा अर्को मिटरब्याजसम्बन्धी जाँचबुझ आयोग गठन ग¥यो । तेजबहादुर नेतृत्वको आयोगमा ३२ हजार उजुरी प¥यो । तर, सबैको प्रभावकारी सुनुवाई हुन सकेन ।

आयोगको काम प्रभाकारी नभएपछि पडितले संघर्ष जारी नै राखे ।पुनः २०८१ फागुन २८ गते सरकारले पूर्व न्यायाधीश बाबुराम रेग्मीको अध्यक्षतामा अर्को तीन सदस्यीय अनुचित लेनदेनसम्बन्धी जाँचबुझ आयोग बनायो ।तेस्रो पटक गठन भएको यो आयोगमा पनि करिब १० हजार उजुरी परे । तर कार्यान्वयन भएन ।

यी आयोगहरू गठन हुनुअघि २०७९ असोज १ गते पनि सरकारले गृह मन्त्रालयका अधिकारी भीष्मराज भुषालको नेतृत्वमा मिटरब्याज अपराध नियन्त्रण सिफारिस कार्यदल गठन भएको थियो । यसपछि मिटरब्याज पीडितहरूले जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालयमा उजुरी दिएका थिए । तर केहीको उजुरी सुनुवाई भएपनि अधिकांशको उजुरीको सुनुवाई नै भएन ।

तेस्रो पैदल मार्च

मिटरब्याज पीडितको तेस्रो पैदल मार्च गत असार २५ गते जनपुरको तिरहुतियागाछीबाट सुरु भएको हो । ३५ जिल्लाका चार सय भन्दा बढी पिडित सहभागी यो यात्रा १५ दिनमा काठमाडौं आइपुग्ने योजना थियो । सरकारले यसअघि सहमति गरि पटक पटक आयोग गठन गरि काम शुरु गरे पनि पूर्णता नदिएपछि उनीहरु आन्दोलित भएका हुन् । निजगढमा रोकिएको उनीहरुको यात्रा माग पूरा नभएपछि तीन दिनपछि पुनः काठमाडौं तर्फ अघि बढ्नेछ ।

मिटरब्याज पीडितको अन्त्यहीन संघर्ष

यसअघि दुइ पटक काठमाडौं सम्मको पैदलमार्च, संघीय सरकारसँग पटक पटक सहमति र तीन तीन वटा आयोग गठन। तर मिटरब्याज पीडितका समस्या ज्युका त्युँ। अनि कहिले प्रचण्ड गर्मी त कहीले झरीका बीच काठमाडौं तर्फको पैदल मार्च ।

मिटरब्याज पीडितहरु यो संघर्षको श्रृखंला माग पूरा नभएसम्म नरोक्ने योजनामा छन् । सरकारसँग पटक पटक सहमति हुने तर कार्यान्यन नहुदाँ उनीहरु पटक पटक आन्दोलनमा उत्रिन बाध्य भएका छन् । मिटरब्याज समस्या समाधानका लागि गृहमन्त्री गुरुङ समक्ष प्रस्तुत गरेका ६ बुँदे मागमाथि प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालयमा छलफलको क्रममा छ ।

अब प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालयको निर्णय आएपछि गृहमन्त्री र मिटरब्याजविरुद्ध किसान–मजदुर आन्दोलनको नेतृत्वबीच पुनः तेस्रो चरणको वार्ता हुनेछ ।

articles.title: नेर र ताजा बस्तीका नागरीकमा खुशी
articles.summary:
मुगु । मुगुको सोरुगाँउपालिका ५ नेरघाटमा मोटरेबल बेली ब्रिज निर्माण सम्पन्न भएपछि यस क्षेत्रका स्थानीयवासीलाई सहज भएको छ । यस पुलले हुम्लाको करिडोरसँग सडक सञ्जाल जोड्दै वर्षौंदेखिको आवतजावतको समस्या समाधान गर्न महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका खेलेको छ । वर्षायाममा खोलामा पानीको बहाव बढ्दा हुने जोखिम र सास्ती पूर्ण रूपमा अन्त्य भएको भन्दै स्थानीय खुसी भएका छन् ।

मुगुको सोरुगाँउपालिका ५ नेरघाटमा बेलिब्रेज पुल निमार्ण भएपछि स्थानीय निकै खुसी भएका छन । पुर्वाधार बिकास कार्यालय मुगुले २०८१साल असार ४ गते ४ करोड ९४ लाखमा ६० मिटर लम्बाई रहेको पुल ठेक्का आह्वान गरेको थियो ।

नेरघाट बेलीब्रेज पुल २०८३ असार मसान्तमा सम्पन्न भएपछि स्थानीयलाई सहज भएको हो । नेर र ताजा गाँउका १ हजार ५ सय भन्दा बढी नागरीकले यो पुलबाट दैनिक आवजावत गर्दछन् । पहिला पुल नहुदा बाबीया (घाँस)को तुईन प्रयोग गरिन्थ्यो । त्यसपछि झोलुङ्गे पुल प्रयोगमा ल्याइयो । झोलुङ्ग पुलबाट पशुचौयाहरुलाई आवतजावत गर्न निकै समस्या हुने गरेको थियो ।

पहिला पुल नहुदा नेर र ताजा गाँउबाट अर्को गाँउ जान ४, ५ घण्टा समय लाग्थ्यो । कर्णाली करीडोर पुग्न निकै कठीन हुनुका साथै गाँउमा उत्पादन गर्ने बस्तुहरुले बजार नपाएर गाँउमै कुहीएर जाने समस्या पनि अन्त्य हुने विश्वास स्थानीयको छ । बेलीब्रीज बनेपछि समय र ढुवानी खर्च दुवै घटेको भन्दै स्थानीयको भनाई छ ।

यो पुलबाट सोरुगाँउपालिका वडा नम्बर ५ नेर र ताजा बस्तीका नागरीकहरुलाई पालिका केन्द्र ,सदरमुकाम, गमगढी ,हुम्ला जिल्लाका बिभिन्न बस्ती र कर्णाली करीडोरबाट सुर्खेत,नेपालगंन्ज जानको लागी निकै सहज भएको छ । साथै गाँउमा कृषकहरुले उत्पादन गरेका रैथाने अन्न बाली लगायत अन्य बस्तुहरुले बजार पाउनुका साथै स्थानीयको आय आर्जनमा पनि सुधार ल्याउने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ ।

मुगुको सदरमुकाम गमगढी र पालिका केन्द्रबाट निकै टाढा रहेको नेर र ताजा बस्तीका नागरीकले पुल नहुदा दैनिक भोग्नु परेको समस्या समाधानको लागी हुम्ला कर्णाली करीडोर र मुगुको नेरघाटमा पुल बनाइएको हो ।

मुगुको नेर र ताजा बस्तीका १५ सय भन्दा बढी नागरीकले दैनिक लाभ लिनुका साथै हुम्ला जिल्लाबासीलाई पनि आवतजावतमा सहज भएको छ ।

कर्णाली प्रदेश पूर्वधार बिकास कार्यालयको आर्थिक सहयोग र स्थानीय सरकारको सहजीकरणमा नेरघाट बेलिब्रेज पुल निमार्ण भएको हो ।

articles.title: ९ बुँदे सहमतिसँगै गणेश नेपाली प्रकरण समाधानतर्फ
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौंको त्रिपुरेश्वरमा आत्मदाह गरेका गणेश नेपालीको शव बुझ्न परिवार सहमत भएको छ । पीडित परिवारसँग आइतबार दोस्रो चरणको वार्तामा सहमति भएपछि परिवार शव बुझ्न सहमत भएको हो । नेपाली परिवार र सरकारबीच नौ बुँदे सहमति भएको छ ।

मुगुको सोरु गाउँपालिका–६ का गणेश नेपालीको आत्मदाहको घटनाको अनुसन्धान गर्न सरकारले पूर्व न्यायाधीशको नेतृत्वमा स्वतन्त्र छानबिन समिति गठन गर्ने भएको छ । सरकार र पीडित पक्षबीच आइतबार ९ बुँदे सहमति भएपछि परिवार शव बुझ्न तयार भएको छ । सहमतिअनुसार पीडितलाई क्षतिपूर्ति उपलब्ध गराइने, शहीद घोषणा सम्बन्धी निर्णय छानबिन प्रतिवेदन, विगतको अभ्यास र प्रचलित कानुनअनुसार गरिने उल्लेख छ ।

सहमति नहुँदा पोस्टमार्टम प्रक्रिया प्रभावित भएको थियो । घटनामा संलग्न भनिएका काठमाडौं महानगर प्रहरीका नगर प्रहरी कर्मचारीलाई अनुसन्धान प्रतिवेदन नआउञ्जेल निलम्बन गरिने सहमति पनि भएको छ । वार्तापछि विवाद समाधानतर्फ उन्मुख भएको सरकारी पक्षले जनाएको छ ।

नेपालीका परिवारसँग भएको ९ सहमतिहरु के के ?

१.यस घटनाको सत्यतथ्य र निष्पक्ष छानबिन गर्न नेपाल सरकारले पूर्वन्यायाधीशको संयोजकत्वमा यथाशीघ्र स्वतन्त्र छानबिन समिति गठन गर्नेछ । उक्त समिति गठन भएको मितिले ७ दिनभित्र प्रतिवेदन नेपाल सरकारसमक्ष पेश गर्नेछ ।।

२.स्वर्गीय गणेश नेपालीलाई सहिद घोषणा गर्ने सम्बन्धमा प्रचलित कानुन, विगतको अभ्यास तथा गठन हुने छानबिन समितिको प्रतिवेदन र सिफारिसका आधारमा नेपाल सरकारले आवश्यक निर्णय प्रक्रिया अगाडि बढाउनेछ ।।

३.घटना घटेको दिन उक्त घटनास्थलमा फिल्डमा अग्रभागमा खटिएका काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकाका महानगरीय प्रहरी बलका कर्मचारीलाई पछि छानबिन आयोगको प्रतिवेदन÷सिफारिस बमोजिम जाने गरी हाललाई निलम्बन गर्न काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकालाई जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय, काठमाडौँबाट लेखी पठाउने ।।

४.काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकाको आगामी बस्ने कार्यपालिका बैठकको निर्णयानुसार मृतककी श्रीमतीलाई निजको योग्यता तथा क्षमताका आधारमा रोजगारी सुनिश्चित गरिनेछ । साथै, मृतककी छोरीको उच्च शिक्षासम्मको अध्ययनका लागि काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकाबाट सम्पूर्ण खर्च समेतको आवश्यक प्रबन्ध मिलाइनेछ । यस कार्यका लागि नेपाल सरकारका सम्बन्धित निकायहरूले समन्वय गर्नेछन् ।

५.काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकाको आगामी कार्यपालिका बैठकबाट निर्णय गराई मृतकको आश्रित परिवारलाई राहतस्वरूप यथोचित रकम उपलब्ध गराइनेछ ।

६.मृतकको अन्तिम संस्कारका लागि आवश्यक पर्ने सम्पूर्ण व्यवस्था तथा काठमाडौँमा गरिने काजक्रियाको आवश्यक व्यवस्थापन काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकाबाट मिलाइनेछ ।

७.पीडित परिवार तथा आफन्तजनको तर्फबाट मृतकको शव बुझिलिने, शव परीक्षण लगायतका कानुनी प्रक्रियामा पूर्ण सहयोग र सहजीकरण गरी सद्गत गर्ने जिम्मा लिइनेछ ।

८. मृतकका एकाघरका परिवारजनको आतेजाते (यातायात) खर्च एवम् काठमाडौंमा काजक्रिया अवधिभर रहँदा–बस्दा हुने सम्पूर्ण खर्चको प्रबन्ध काठमाडौं महानगरपालिकाले व्यहोर्नेछ ।

९.पीडित परिवारका एकाघरका परिवारको स्वास्थ्य बीमाको कार्य स्वास्थ्य तथा खाद्य स्वच्छता मन्त्रालयबाट आवश्यक व्यवस्था मिलाइनेछ ।।

घटनाको सत्यतथ्य छानबिन समितिको निष्कर्षका आधारमा दोषी देखिएकामाथि थप कारबाही प्रक्रिया अघि बढाइने सहमति भएको छ । तर परिवारले राहत स्वरुप कति रकम पाउने भन्ने खुलाइएको छैन । पिडित परिवारको सहमतिमा उनीहरुको माग अनुसारकै रकम दिईने बताईएको छ ।

सम्झौता गर्न गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङ जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय, काठमाडौं पुगेका थिए भने नेपालीको परिवारबाट श्रीमती एकमाया नेपाली, दाइ मदन नेपालीसहित हिक्मत शाही, धर्मराज शाही, मुगुका सांसद खड्गबहादुर शाही लगायत थिए । यसअघि काठमाडौं महानगरपालिकाले गणेशको परिवारलाई रोजगारी र निःशुल्क शिक्षाको जिम्मेवारी लिने घोषणा गरेको थियो ।

गणेशको मृत्युबारे उपत्यका प्रहरी कार्यालय, रानीपोखरीका डीआईजी गोविन्द थपलियाको नेतृत्वको पाँच सदस्यीय समितिले पनि छानबिन गरिरहेको छ । पिडित पक्षबाट १२ जना र सरकारको पक्षबाट चार जनाले सहमतिमा हस्ताक्षर गरेका छन् । पीडित पक्ष र सरकारी टोलीबीच काठमाडौं जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालयमा करिब २४ घण्टा लामो वार्ता भए पछि मात्र सहमति जुटेको हो ।

articles.title: New rules outlaw forced haircuts at schools, but schools aren’t convinced
articles.summary:
Sambriddha Karki, 18, had barely finished six months of his grade 11 when he experienced the forced haircut. Every three to four weeks, teachers and discipline in-charges at his school in Kathmandu would line students up and check their hair. If it was too long, the punishments varied: a phone call home, a class he wasn’t allowed to enter, sometimes his identity card was taken away.

“They were giving me a lot of mental harassment for getting my hair cut,” said Karki. The reason given, he said, was always the same that students needed a “professional look.” He didn’t buy it. “Whether you cut your hair or not doesn’t change anything. It doesn’t make your studies better or worse.”

So he did what he’d watched a civic platform called SpeakUp Nepal do with other complaints. Take a small, local grievance and push it forward. He filed a petition. In the first month. It drew 250 signatures.

That’s roughly the threshold that turns an ordinary complaint into a campaign, according to Kritika Ghimire, project manager at SpeakUp Nepal—one of just three people, alongside Prince Shah and Sahara Bhandari, who run the platform. “We don’t decide which petitions deserve attention. That’s decided by the public,” she said. Under the platform’s policy, any petition that garners 250 verified supporters is automatically forwarded to the relevant government authority. When Karki’s petition crossed that threshold within its first month, Ghimire said, “That was the moment we realised this wasn’t just one student’s experience as hundreds of people were saying, ‘This matters to us.’”

From there, the petition moved institution to institution over roughly 19 months, the Kathmandu Education Office, the Centre for Education and Human Resource Development, and eventually the Ministry of Education and Sports, building into the tenth amendment to the education regulations on July 3.

The amendment bars schools and colleges from forcibly cutting students' hair without their consent. It also broadens protections for students' personal appearance by prohibiting discrimination or harassment over hairstyles, body image or makeup, and outlaws physical and mental harassment carried out in the name of school discipline. It is the first legal provision explicitly stating a student’s appearance belongs to the student, not the institution.

Karki said many schools and colleges around Kathmandu haven’t stopped the practice, weeks after the amendment’s passage. “Many schools are still not following it,” he said. “Only one or two colleges have stopped it, but unofficially, they are still compelling students.”

For Ariana, a student at Budhanilkantha School, who the Post is identifying with a pseudonym to protect her privacy, the amendment’s focus on hair doesn’t touch the unequal freedoms and expectations she says still shape daily life at her school. Her school has no formal rulebook on appearance, she said, but teachers expect girls to keep their hair tied, wear no makeup, and skip mehendi. She likes wearing light makeup which includes mascara, lip gloss and said there’s no organised “shaming environment” around it, but female teachers have called her out in front of other students when they notice it. “Makeup is about feeling good about yourself,” she said. “It shouldn’t be such a big deal.”

Bharat Prasai, 39, the father of a nine-year-old, said policing students' appearance has persisted across generations. And the real problem is that there’s never been a clear, consistent standard in the first place. He recalled his own school days, when teachers measured hair length by pulling it.

Looking at it now as a parent rather than a student, he doesn’t see the harm in hair falling below the neck or over the forehead or girls just putting makeup on. “I don’t think it should be a problem,” he said, adding that he doesn’t believe teachers should have the authority to police it either way.

The campaign’s biggest early obstacle, Ghimire said, wasn’t any single institution. It was persuading people that the issue deserved policy attention in the first place. “For many, it had simply been accepted as a normal part of school discipline for years,” she said. “We spent a lot of time explaining that this wasn’t about hairstyles or challenging school discipline, it was about whether forced haircuts were an appropriate disciplinary practice.”

Once that shifted, the campaign still had to work its way through the ordinary friction of policymaking—legal reviews and inter-agency coordination, which Ghimire said resulted in long stretches when progress seemed to stall. She said neither SpeakUp Nepal nor the original petitioner faced significant pushback or ridicule over the 19 months, describing most engagement with schools, officials and parents as respectful, even where opinions differed.

Ghimire said, “Petitions are escalated automatically once they cross the public-support threshold, regardless of the topic or who is in government.” She said the amendment is not the finish line. SpeakUp Nepal’s next goal is to see the same protection enshrined in the Education Act rather than left to regulations alone. The organisation is working with the ministry and CEHRD to build a formal complaint and reporting mechanism, an acknowledgment, she said, that “no law is complete without effective implementation.”

“Success won’t simply be measured by a policy change,” she said. “It will be measured by whether students across Nepal genuinely experience that change in their daily school lives.”

Not everyone in the school system agrees the law should exist at all. Navraj Bhatta, the president of PABSON district chapter Kathmandu, argued that hair, dress and grooming should remain a matter between school and parents, not something legislated by the state.

“The government should not entertain this or make hair a prestige issue,” Bhatta said. “An institution must make its own rules and regulations.” He said PABSON’s official position, clarified at a recent press conference with three other umbrella organisations representing Nepal's private education sector—HISSAN, APEN and NPABSON—is that the government overstepped: “It’s not right for the government to interfere in this matter.”

Bhatta acknowledged that compliance has been uneven since the ban. “Just the other day in my school, students hadn’t got their hair cut,” he said. “When I told them to cut it, the students took to social media saying it was against the rules.” He argued that the change has emboldened students rather than resolving the issue. “It encourages students to be defiant. Since it’s banned, it will cause behavioral issues.”

Kalpana Oli Sitaula, school incharge of Pathibhara Academy in Bhaktapur, offered a different perspective on the same discomfort. She framed appearance rules as part of a broader disciplinary structure schools rely on, especially as class sizes shrink and children arrive with less experience of being told “no” at home.

“In a mass setting, we can’t always say ‘yes’ to everything,” she said, adding that individual counselling is increasingly replacing the blanket rules schools used to rely on. She did not defend forced haircuts outright, but described the shift as something schools would need time to absorb. “These issues will continue to arise for a year or two,” she said. “We have been following one system, and moving to another will naturally involve a transitional period.”

Sitaula said she doesn’t think the change should be resisted simply because it’s new. “If it becomes law, we must obey it,” she said. “We teachers also need to change along with the students.” At the same time, she cautioned against treating hair as disconnected from everything else a school monitors. She said, “Hair doesn’t determine everything, but we have to watch what else is added to it, like behavioural activities.”

The education ministry maintains that the change is neither optional nor temporary. Shiva Kumar Sapkota, spokesperson at the ministry, rejected the idea that a regulation amendment as opposed to an Act promulgated by the parliament leaves the protection vulnerable to reversal. “Any legal provision made for student well-being, student rights, student freedom, and creating a proper learning atmosphere is permanent,” he said.

Asked how the ministry intends to enforce the rule against schools like the ones Karki and Bhatta described, Sapkota said violations now carry legal consequences. “Once it becomes a legal provision, any violation is punishable,” he said. “If someone does not enforce it, a case can be filed in court or administrative action can be taken.” He said monitoring will largely sit with local governments, much as Kathmandu Metropolitan City already runs a dedicated helpline, and that no grace period had been built in for schools to adjust. “There is no need for a timeline,” he said. “From the day it was published in the Nepal Gazette, it has been in force.”

Raju Ghimire, a child activist and deputy director at Voice of Children, said the legal foundation is weaker than it looks as it came as a Cabinet-approved regulation rather than legislation passed by parliament. As a result, he said, it carries less legal weight. “Since it’s not an Act, it might not be as binding, although it is supposed to be,” Ghimire said.

He is also critical of how the policy came together. “The government should have consulted organisations like us first,” he said, calling the process one-sided. “If policymaking is one-sided, you get these reactions.” He echoed Kritika Ghimire’s emphasis on implementation, saying awareness, rather than more rules, is the immediate need. “Awareness of the rules is the first step towards effective implementation,” he said.

articles.title: Government to relocate Valley squatters to home districts
articles.summary:
The government has begun relocating landless squatters displaced from the riverbanks of the Kathmandu Valley to their permanent home districts, saying there is little land available within the Capital for their resettlement.

The move comes as authorities continue clearing settlements along the Bagmati river corridor, displacing hundreds of families who have lived in Kathmandu for decades and leaving many uncertain about where they will rebuild their lives.

The relocation process follows directives from the Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives and Poverty Alleviation and relies on digital land ownership records compiled by the High-Powered Committee for Integrated Development of the Bagmati Civilisation.

To identify genuine landless households, the Department of Land Management and Archive cross-checked applicants through the Land Records Information Management System (LRIMS), verifying whether they own land anywhere in the country. Those found to have no registered land are being referred to their home districts for land allocation under existing laws, while those with property elsewhere are disqualified.

Balbhandra Banstola, chairperson of the National Land Commission, said official correspondence has already been sent to local authorities to facilitate land allocation for 28 families in their home districts.

“We search the land registry across all 77 districts to determine whether an applicant owns property,” Banstola told Kantipur. “If someone is found to own land elsewhere, they no longer meet the legal definition of a landless squatter and are therefore ineligible for state land.”

According to the commission, six families have so far been disqualified after land registered in their names was discovered in other districts.

Banstola said the verification process is still under way and has yet to cover all displaced households.

“For those who are confirmed to have no land anywhere in the country, we are moving ahead with the process,” he said. “Once verification is complete, people whose citizenship was issued outside the Valley will be referred to their home districts for resettlement. We hope to complete most of the verification within this month.”

He acknowledged that providing land within Kathmandu Valley is virtually impossible because local governments have no land to spare.

“The metropolitan cities and municipalities of Kathmandu, Lalitpur and Bhaktapur have informed us that they do not have land available for distribution,” Banstola said. “Given this constraint, we have proposed an integrated housing model as an alternative for landless families who cannot be accommodated within the Valley.”

The National Land Commission published its first list of verified beneficiaries on July 16, identifying 14 people with no registered land anywhere in Nepal. Their files have already been forwarded to the relevant district authorities to begin the land allocation process.

The first list includes Kumal Ghalan and Arjun Syangtan of Makawanpur, Madan Kami of Taplejung, Rajesh Majhi of Morang, Achhelal Paswan of Rautahat, Pabita Thapa Magar of Dhankuta, Jiban Kumar Pahari of Sindhuli, Niraj Thapa of Sindhupalchok, Rabbani Ansari of Mahottari, Som Bahadur Nepali of Kathmandu, Apsara Damai of Bhojpur, Harkil Giri of Sunsari, Tek Bahadur Layo of Dhanusha, and Jitman Tamang of Sarlahi.

For many of those on the list, however, the prospect of returning to districts they left years or even decades ago has brought anxiety rather than relief.

Kumar Ghalan, 46, learnt through Facebook that his name had appeared on the list. Days later, he received a phone call from Bagmati Rural Municipality in Makawanpur informing him that land would be allocated there.

Ghalan moved to Kathmandu with his parents as a child and grew up in the Thapathali squatter settlement. His two children were born and raised in the capital. His daughter is in the first year of university and his son studies in Grade Four.

“They told me I would receive land in Ward 8, but local officials are still looking for a suitable plot,” Ghalan said after travelling to Makawanpur.

He said he had hoped to be settled somewhere near Kathmandu because his family's life is rooted in the capital.

“My children study in Kathmandu, and we have lived here all our lives. Starting over in a rural area and finding work will be extremely difficult,” he said. “I have explained our situation to the local authorities, but I don't know what decision they will make.”

Pabita Thapa Magar, 45, who is staying at the Kharipati holding centre in Bhaktapur after being evicted from the riverbanks, said she discovered through social media that she had also been selected for relocation.

Although her citizenship certificate lists Dhankuta as her permanent address, she said she has never visited the district.

“I have not received an official call yet,” she said. “I have never been to Dhankuta and have no idea how I will survive if I am sent there. There are no jobs for us. If we have to leave Kathmandu, starting life again will be very difficult.”

The amount of land allocated to beneficiaries is governed by the Land Rules 2021 (19th Amendment).

Under the rules, verified landless Dalits and landless squatters are entitled to up to 130 square metres of residential land free of cost within Kathmandu Valley, metropolitan cities, sub-metropolitan cities and municipalities. Outside these urban areas, they can receive up to 300 square metres for housing.

For agricultural purposes, beneficiaries are entitled to up to 2,000 square metres in the Tarai and Inner Tarai and up to 3,000 square metres in the hills and mountains.

Unregulated settlers are eligible for up to 130 square metres of residential land in Kathmandu Valley and other urban areas, and up to 1,000 square metres elsewhere, subject to payment of the prescribed government revenue.

Banstola said land would be distributed strictly in accordance with these provisions. He added that the commission had streamlined administrative procedures to speed up the issuance of land ownership certificates.

“On the day we forward the files to district committees, we also hold virtual meetings instructing them to treat these cases as a priority,” he said. “The Ministry of Home Affairs has also directed Chief District Officers to handle the process with urgency. If beneficiaries cooperate with the local committees, they should be able to receive their land ownership certificates within two to three months.”

articles.title: These seven Nepali startups are building technology that tackles real-world problems
articles.summary:
Nepali youth have unveiled seven unique digital platforms to tackle societal challenges across healthcare, education, tourism, agriculture, accessibility, and finance. These creative solutions emerged prominently during the recently concluded ‘Code for Impact’ hackathon, an intensive entrepreneurial challenge jointly organised by the United States Embassy in Nepal and Adhyanta Advisory.

The event drew 190 companies from across the country, each pitching unique technological interventions to address pressing systemic hurdles. The primary purpose behind this major national initiative was to actively connect digital infrastructure with everyday human challenges, transforming abstract programming into practical tools for social good.

Following rigorous evaluations, seven exceptional groups were declared national winners, showcasing the immense potential of homegrown technology. Among these innovators, Aashirbad Care, NepAI, Data Hiti, and Synaptic emerged at the very top, securing national titles along with substantial cash prizes to scale their operational models.

The success of these young innovators comes at a critical time for Nepal’s IT sector. The digital ecosystem faces policy ambiguities, lack of venture capital, and a continuous brain drain of software developers seeking opportunities abroad. Yet, events like ‘Code for Impact’ show that local talent remains resilient and capable of engineering world-class solutions tailored specifically to Nepal’s unique geographical and socio-economic realities.

During the award distribution ceremony, Mike Harker, public affairs chief at the US Embassy in Kathmandu who served as a member of the jury, praised the remarkable ingenuity of the participants. He said that the strategic partnership between creative Nepali youth and advanced American technological concepts could open unprecedented frontiers for local economic development.

Harker masterfully compared the difficult journey of modern entrepreneurship to climbing Mount Everest, reminding the audience that reaching the summit is merely half the battle. He said true success requires solid partnerships and thorough preparation rather than solitary efforts.

Stuti Basnyat, co-founder of Adhyanta Advisory, stated that the ultimate achievement of the entire programme lies in its direct ability to bridge the gap between advanced technology and the actual, practical difficulties faced by ordinary citizens. Adding to this, Kailash Bijayanand, president of the American Chamber of Commerce (AmCham) in Nepal, observed that the participating startups have genuinely strived to discover meaningful solutions that carry a profoundly positive and lasting impact on the daily lives of the people.

Aashirbad Care: support for senior citizens

Addressing the critical gaps within the country’s healthcare system, Aashirbad Care has formally launched an essential digital service to provide comprehensive medical treatment, rehabilitation, and compassionate caregiving directly at the doorsteps of elderly citizens.

This startup targets senior citizens who are suffering from chronic illnesses or dealing with advanced age-related frailties. Dr Rohit Rawat, co-founder of the company, explained that the platform was conceived directly in response to Nepal’s shifting demographic trends, characterised by a rapidly growing elderly population and a simultaneous rise in complex geopolitical health complications.

Dr Rawat, who simultaneously works in the clinical department of Patan Academy of Health Sciences, explained that Aashirbad Care operates fundamentally as a technology-driven care coordination platform designed entirely by a professional team of certified medical doctors. “We noticed a severe lack of structured post-hospitalisation care in Nepali households, which often leads to preventable readmissions,” said Dr Rawat.

The service fees for caregivers are carefully determined based on the specific clinical condition and personal requirements of each individual patient. To maintain operational viability, the company requires a minimum booking shift of eight hours. For standard, non-clinical companionship and basic care, the platform charges a modest fee of Rs100 per hour. However, for patients requiring specialised medical attention—such as nasogastric feeding, regular secretion suctioning, or advanced dementia management—the cost scales up to Rs150 per hour.

The startup began as a modest initiative by Dr Rawat and Pratik Gautam, who initially invested a personal sum of Rs500,000 to build the basic software infrastructure. Today, the enterprise has rapidly expanded into a robust professional team consisting of 57 dedicated individuals, including Dr Sitanshu Dhakal and Prabesh Gautam. The platform now features 50 fully trained, verified caregivers who provide round-the-clock assistance across all three districts of the Kathmandu Valley—Kathmandu, Lalitpur and Bhaktapur.

Recognising further gaps in traditional hospital settings, the organisation has recently introduced an innovative ‘Hospital Assistance Service’ to support families who are unable to stay overnight with hospitalised relatives. Dr Rawat noted that the public demand and popularity for this specific service have surged tremendously within a very short period. “It has been only about two months since we initiated this hospital assistant service, and it is becoming exceptionally popular among urban families,” shared Dr Rawat. “So far, our trained assistants have successfully provided dedicated bedside care to ten major clients across reputable institutions like the BP Smriti Hospital, the Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital, and the Patan Hospital. For this vital assistance, we charge a reasonable rate ranging from Rs110 to Rs 120per hour.”

NepAI: Braille now in Unicode as well

The ‘Access Code’ team from Pokhara, comprising Arun Shrestha, Chhabi Ale, Rohan Raj Paudel, and Dhiraj Chaurasiya, developed ‘NepAI’ to convert Braille into Unicode text.

As Ale is visually impaired himself, the technology was built on the foundation of his personal experiences. He has been working on preparing the essential Braille datasets required for the application. “When teachers or parents cannot understand what students have written in Braille, the learning process slows down drastically,” says Ale. “We write in Braille and take our exams in Braille, but because there are no transcribers to convert those materials into standard text, we are forced to wait for weeks just to have our papers marked and to receive feedback.”

There are more than 145,000 blind people in Nepal. Banks have consistently hesitated to allow them to open bank accounts, make payments, provide signatures, or access banking applications. Given this situation, Ale expects the Braille-to-Unicode technology to make things much easier.

“This will also become an effective medium for employers who want to hire visually impaired individuals but hesitate due to communication gaps,” he said. “It will broaden our employment opportunities. Organisations like the Nepal Association of the Blind and the National Federation of the Disabled Nepal can use this institutionally for the educational and professional development of their members.” Providing paid services through Access Code is the team's business model.

Data Hiti: easing cross-border transactions

Operating in the digital payments sector, Data Hiti aims to streamline cross-border transactions. According to its co-founder Kabish Pokharel, the team had already been developing international products. However, after facing severe difficulties in receiving payments from abroad, they sought a solution, which led to the concept of the Elytra app.

“We make cross-border payments fast and efficient, and we are currently providing payment services for American companies operating in Nepal to bring their funds into the country,” said Pokharel. “Data Hiti has developed an instant-settlement technology as an alternative to the traditional banking system.” The team includes Pokharel alongside Anshu Regmi and Rij Maharjan.

According to Pokharel, the Elytra app settles cross-border transactions within a few minutes using a ‘non-custodial ABI’. He claimed this technology immediately resolves the issues of ‘pre-funding’ and the days-long delays associated with receiving remittance through traditional banking. “We are not a remittance company or a payment service provider ourselves,” Pokharel clarified. “We are simply a technology firm. We provide technical services to licensed banks and financial institutions. Our product is designed to serve existing fintech giants rather than compete with them.”

Cad Coder: from medicine search to appointments

Addressing persistent issues in the healthcare sector, a team comprising Bishal Sharma, Ritesh Raut, Prasatab Shrestha, and Samisha Yonghang from Jhapa has developed a platform called Dose. The startup integrates patients, doctors, hospitals, and pharmacies into a single network.

Bishal explained that the platform provides transparent information in a Nepali context where accessing details about medicines and healthcare services is typically cumbersome. “Health records are fragmented and inaccessible. Patients cannot easily identify authentic medicines, compare prices, or find doctors,” he said. “Dose offers users the convenience of searching for medicines, comparing prices, and booking hospital appointments all in one place.”

To prevent the haphazard use of medicines, the platform includes a prescription verification feature. Cad Coder stated that its technology utilises modern software infrastructure, including Dingo and LangChain. The startup is currently expanding its network by partnering with hospitals and pharmacies.

Neptu: original experiences for tourists

In the tourism sector, ‘Neptu’ uses artificial intelligence to help tourists discover new and overlooked destinations. This hyper-local tourism application primarily helps foreign tourists understand local experiences in Nepal and generates travel itineraries for them, according to Neptu’s business lead, Alisha Hada.

“The app does not have all its features integrated just yet, but the AI itinerary and information on local places are available,” said Hada. “In just a while, tourists will be able to book local guides directly through the app. We will arrange for local guides to show tourists around during cultural events such as Holi, jatras, or mud festivals. We also plan to package experiences like tasting local cuisine and making Bhaktapur's traditional clay pottery for tourists.”

Subodh Kathayat conceptualised Neptu in 2022. Studying at the New Jersey Institute of Technology in the US, Subodh and Alisha formed a team with Dhiraj KC and Keshav Thapa.

Synaptic: a companion for autistic children

Meanwhile, ‘Synaptic’ has created an environment for children with autism, learning difficulties, or speech delays to learn vocabulary using augmented reality (AR) technology. Developed by Kathmandu University students Arya Pathak, Himesh Dulal, Safal Narsingh Shrestha, Shoham Kayastha, and Shreyan Basti, the ‘Card AI’ app transforms physical learning cards into 3D visuals and audio through AR.

“When a physical card is scanned through our app, a 3D model of the respective animal or object appears,” said Pathak. “Additionally, voices and natural sounds are audible in both Nepali and English, allowing children to easily learn words as if they are playing with toys.”

Pathak said while Nepal lacks official and reliable government statistics on autism, indicators from the World Health Organisation and neighbouring countries suggest that around 300,000 children are affected in Nepal. To address this serious issue, the team has been collaborating with Tribhuvan University’s Cognitive Science and Psycholinguistics Lab and the Hope Care Centre for Child Development and Research Centre for the past year. Their initial prototype is currently being tested by one teacher, three parents, and six therapists.

Mithila Coder: the farmer’s advisor

Janakpur’s ‘Mithila Coder’ is providing agricultural consultancy to farmers in local languages. The ‘AgriSense’ app, developed by this startup, guides farmers like an expert from the time seeds are sown until the harvest. Amardeep Soni told Kantipur that the team designed the app to fetch soil details and weather data from the Nepal Agricultural Research Council (NARC) to offer concrete recommendations on which crops are best suited for specific plots of land.

The group consists of developers Amardeep, Purushottam Yadav, Shyam Sundar Yadav, and Satyanarayan Sah. “All four of us are developers and we are also farmers ourselves, so this was our own family problem,” said Soni. “Farmers in the Tarai still farm the traditional way and are forced to work based on guesswork, which is why we are building the AgriSense app. We aim to use technology to solve the problems farmers face due to a lack of experts.” He added that if a crop contracts a disease, farmers can simply send a photo, and the app will use AI to diagnose the issue and suggest treatments.

articles.title: Foreign tourists are staying longer, but spending less in Nepal
articles.summary:
Foreign tourists are staying in Nepal longer than ever, but they are spending less each day, raising fresh concerns about the country’s ability to attract high-value visitors despite a surge in investment in luxury hotels and resorts.

According to government statistics, the average length of stay of foreign tourists reached a record 16.34 days in 2025. However, their average daily spending fell to $33.09, the second-lowest level on record and far below the regional average of $100-150.

The figures highlight a growing mismatch in Nepal’s tourism industry. While visitors are extending their trips, largely due to trekking, mountaineering and leisure travel, businesses say the country is failing to convert longer stays into higher tourism earnings.

Tourism ministry data shows tourist spending has been on a long downward trend since peaking at $79.1 per day in 2003.

The lowest spending on record was $31.9 in 1996, when Nepal received 393,613 tourists. This was the time when the Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist) launched an armed “People’s War” against the government to overthrow the constitutional monarchy and establish a communist republic. Led by Pushpa Kamal Dahal, the Maoists initiated the conflict by launching simultaneous attacks on police posts across multiple districts.

The tourism ministry said the latest length-of-stay figures now are more reliable because, from 2025 onwards, they are generated through a centralised electronic tourism management information system rather than traditional estimation methods.

According to the ministry, the record stay indicates that tourists are spending more time exploring Nepal’s natural and cultural attractions, supported by improved tourism services and better promotion.

Longer stays are generally considered a positive indicator because visitors spend more on accommodation, food, transport and activities, boosting the economy.

But hoteliers say the expected financial gains have not materialised.

“To be honest, our airspace and roads are not safe and, as a result, rich tourists normally avoid visiting Nepal,” said hotelier Yogendra Shakya. “If we want to attract tourists who spend more, the first reform should be in the transport sector.”

He said Nepal now has luxury resorts and hotels comparable to international standards, but safety concerns continue to discourage affluent travellers.

Nepal has remained on the European Commission’s air safety blacklist since December 2013, preventing Nepali airlines from operating in European skies and reinforcing concerns over aviation safety.

In 2025, Nepal welcomed 1.05 million foreign tourists, of whom 91 percent arrived by air, underlining the country’s heavy dependence on air connectivity. Another 146,630 visitors entered through land border points.

Despite crossing the one-million mark for the third consecutive year, arrivals have yet to recover to the pre-pandemic level recorded in 2019.

Tourism entrepreneurs say recurring plane crashes, poor highway infrastructure and weak international promotion continue to undermine Nepal’s competitiveness.

At the same time, Nepal has witnessed a wave of investment in high-end hospitality.

Luxury properties including Shinta Mani Mustang, Dusit Thani Himalayan Resort & Spa, The Terraces Resort & Spa in Lakuri Bhanjyang and Kavya Resort in Nagarkot have opened in recent years, with more projects under development.

Marriott International, in partnership with CG Hospitality, is also developing two ultra-luxury hotels in Kathmandu, including a Rs15 billion Ritz-Carlton in Thamel.

However, many of these running properties have struggled to achieve expected occupancy levels.

Hoteliers say aviation accidents, road safety concerns, political instability and last year’s Gen Z protests during the peak autumn tourism season significantly hurt bookings and tourist spending.

An official at Dusit Thani Himalayan Resort & Spa, requesting anonymity, said the resort faced severe challenges during and after the Gen Z protests.

“We have recovered now,” the official said. “Wedding and anniversary celebrations, mostly from India, have increased. Indian guests usually book three-night packages.”

Industry insiders say Nepal has enormous potential in the luxury tourism segment, but repeated natural disasters, aviation accidents and political unrest continue to erode traveller confidence.

Mid-range hotels, meanwhile, remain less dependent on foreign arrivals as they continue to rely heavily on domestic travellers.

Shakya said the growing number of Indian visitors, many travelling for trekking and mountaineering, has contributed to the longer average stay.

“But we still doubt whether all the money they [Indian] spend in Nepal is formally channelled through the banking system, particularly spending on shopping, restaurants and local transport,” he said.

Mani Raj Lamichhane, director of the Nepal Tourism Board, attributed the decline in daily spending partly to the appreciation of the US dollar against the Nepali rupee, which has made Nepal cheaper for international tourists.

“The rapid increase in the number of hotels and resorts has also intensified unhealthy price competition,” Lamichhane said.

Luxury hotels, in particular, continue to offer rooms at rates significantly below pre-pandemic levels in an effort to attract guests.

Nepal currently has more than 1,600 hotels capable of offering around 64,000 room nights, including 222 star-rated properties.

According to the government’s latest report, travel remained Nepal’s largest service export in fiscal year 2024-25, generating Rs88.66 billion and accounting for 37.15 percent of total service exports.

However, as global uncertainty persists, including the conflict in West Asia, Nepal’s tourism industry has become increasingly reliant on domestic travellers while spending by international visitors has remained largely stagnant at pre-Covid levels.

Shakya said hotels and resorts around the Kathmandu Valley and in other destinations now depend heavily on Nepali guests to sustain operations.

He also pointed to broader global economic factors behind weaker visitor spending.

Inflation has eroded household purchasing power worldwide, encouraging tourists to take more budget-conscious trips. Rising airfare and fuel costs have also forced travellers to cut spending on accommodation and dining, while the growing popularity of short-term trips has diverted business away from full-service hotels.

“As a result of the rising airfare, the number of Indian tourists has reached record levels in Nepal and they are staying longer,” Shakya said.

The ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party has pledged to double annual tourist arrivals to around 2.5 million and significantly increase tourism earnings within five years.

Tourism entrepreneurs say private investment in hotels and resorts continues to pour into the sector, but unless the government improves transport safety, infrastructure and destination promotion, filling thousands of newly built rooms with high-spending international visitors will remain a daunting challenge.

articles.title: Rebuilding Nepal’s judiciary means spreading power to the provinces
articles.summary:
The fallout from the Gen Z protests of last September has reduced Nepal’s courtrooms to administrative and architectural ruin, exposing their fundamental fragility. The scale of the destruction during the protests is staggering, yet the subsequent standstill of the legal system suggests that the crisis is as much structural as it is physical. If the state is to restore the rule of law, it cannot do so simply by rebuilding the infrastructure. It must radically decentralise the seat of justice.

The statistics released for fiscal year 2025-26 represent an unprecedented collapse in judicial output. The national case clearance rate, which stood at 65.69 percent in the previous year, has plummeted to a mere 55 percent. Out of 357,023 pending cases across all tiers, only 196,474 were settled, leaving a backlog of 160,549 disputes unresolved. The Supreme Court, the ultimate arbiter of the law, recorded its lowest performance in history, disposing of only 29.46 percent of its caseload, plummeting 12.54 percentage points from the previous fiscal year. This failure is the result of a system that has been physically and technologically decapitated.

The physical carnage of the Gen Z protests is quantified in billions of rupees. Protesters targeted 23 court premises, leaving ten buildings completely destroyed and nine others partially ruined. The Supreme Court’s historical building, a symbol of the nation’s legal heritage, alone suffered damages worth Rs1.23 billion. Beyond the masonry, the loss of 936,000 legal files and documents represents an irreparable erasure of legal history. When the arson attacks consumed these papers, they effectively halted thousands of ongoing litigations, plunging the nation into a state where justice is not only delayed but, for many, entirely extinguished.

The technological fallout was equally catastrophic. The destruction of central servers during the riots caused a nationwide system failure that even untouched courts could not escape. The Patan High Court, for instance, saw its operations frozen for two months due to the loss of central databases, despite its physical premises remaining intact. Judicial activities across the country remained suspended for nearly four months. This reliance on a centralised digital and physical hub in the capital has proven to be a strategic vulnerability. While individual judges demonstrated remarkable resilience by maintaining high disposal rates through personal initiative, the system they serve remains fundamentally broken.

The current model of judicial centralisation is no longer tenable. To prevent a single point of failure from again crippling the entire judiciary, the state must look toward structural reforms that are not mentioned in the immediate reports but are necessitated by the current quagmire. A remedy lies in elevating the High Courts to the status of courts of record. At present, the Supreme Court is overwhelmed by a massive volume of routine appeals that could, and should, be finalised at lower levels. By making the High Courts a court of record, their judgments would carry a definitive authority, and their archives would serve as permanent, legally binding evidence. If each High Court were a self-contained repository of legal history, the destruction of a central server or a central building would no longer result in nationwide paralysis. This shift would naturally decrease the caseload of the Supreme Court, allowing it to focus exclusively on constitutional interpretation and matters of national importance. Another viable alternative is hiring ad hoc judges, similar to the new practice in India, to decrease the caseload on each judge.

The path to recovery requires more than just the Rs2.8 billion needed for physical reconstruction. The state must invest in distributed digital backups and empower lower courts to act as final arbiters in the majority of minor civil disputes. The rule of fire was able to halt the rule of law because the latter was concentrated in too few buildings and too few servers. To rebuild the Supreme Court without relaxing its burden is to invite the next catastrophe. The judiciary must be restructured so that even if the centre is struck, the scales of justice continue to balance in every province.

articles.title: Nepal’s loneliest generation
articles.summary:
A generation of Nepali children is growing up healthier, better schooled than any before it and also the loneliest. This paradox belongs at the centre of our new government’s thinking, yet it is entirely absent from national conversation. We count enrollment, literacy and remittances, but fail to ask whether the web of caring adults, on which every childhood depends, is holding or fraying.

My four decades of work on child development across three continents revealed one pattern: Development brings survival and schooling, then inadvertently and quietly strips away the human bonds essential to children’s wellbeing. The Nepal I grew up in was desperately poor by most economic measures, but its children were rarely alone. Families were extended, cousins filled courtyards and neighbours claimed the right to scold a misbehaving child, an extension of what Donald Winnicott called a ‘safe holding environment’. That web was an infrastructure, as real as any road or health clinic.

40 years of development transformed survival. A Nepali child born today will live 20 years longer than her grandmother. But the courtyards are quieter now. More than 3.5 million Nepalis—one in eight—work abroad; remittances exceed a quarter of GDP. According to UNICEF, in any classroom of 30, six children have a parent abroad and two live with neither parent. The familial structures and networks that once held us are hollowing out.

Some will call this the price of progress. Common sense might agree until one examines the evidence. The Harvard Study of Adult Development, after eight decades of following thousands of lives, concluded, in Robert Waldinger’s words: “Good relationships keep us happier and healthier. Period.” Not income or achievement. Surgeon General Vivek Murthy prices disconnection in terms no economist can wave away: A toll rivalling 15 cigarettes a day. There is evidence that left-behind children in Nepal, China and the Philippines show more loneliness, anxiety and weaker school performance. By 2015, a third of Nepali adolescents reported frequent loneliness, and 13.6 percent had seriously considered suicide. None of this is the fault of parents who leave; most board that flight out of desperation and love. But cash wired from Doha is no substitute for a father’s presence at dinner. That loss is immense, yet uncounted. It belongs on the same scale as GDP because it is development, or its undoing.

Nor is this a symptom that wealth and growth will cure, as some economists continue to espouse. In the US, children living with two parents fell from 85 percent in 1968 to 70 percent. Adults with no close friends tripled between 1990 and 2020. In 2023, 40 percent of American high schoolers reported persistent sadness or hopelessness, a record. Prosperity did not protect American children. It masked their crisis. In 2025, the World Health Organisation called teenagers the world’s loneliest age group. Karl Polanyi named the mechanism 80 years ago: When market logic expands into every corner of life, it erodes bonds no market can price. In wealthy nations, that erosion took generations. In Nepal, we are compressing it into one. This is no argument against markets, which have lifted more people out of poverty than any other system in history. It is an argument for setting their boundaries.

Nowhere are the stakes sharper than in digital space and social media, which have added steroids to adolescents’ loneliness and fragility. A clumsy ban on it helped ignite the Gen Z uprising of September 2025. Our young people rose to defend their right to connect, and they were right to. Yet, that technology is reshaping childhood in ways barely reckoned with. Mobile ownership exceeds 90 percent of households. A child in a remote village sees the same algorithmic feeds as a teenager in Kathmandu or Chicago, engineered to hold attention whatever the cost to a developing mind. Research increasingly links heavy social media use to adolescent loneliness and isolation. Those online for more than three hours daily face roughly double the risk of poor mental health. We are raising a generation more connected and, at once, more fragile.

The lesson is not the false choice between banning technology and surrendering to it. Digital access opens learning, opportunity and voice. But digital progress without care for children is no progress at all. Nepal holds a rare advantage—we need not wait two decades for others to tell us what to do after the damage is done. By early 2026, 114 countries, over half worldwide, restricted smartphones in schools, up from a quarter three years before. Finland, for example, has legislated device limits and is restoring teacher-led instruction. Australia sets a minimum age for social media usage. Childhood is being reclaimed as a public interest, not a design choice left to profit-driven platforms.

Beneath the screens lies a deeper reform: the purpose of school itself. Education in Nepal, as elsewhere, has narrowed from forming citizens to producing workers, leaving children rarely taught to navigate loss, listen across differences, manage conflict or sustain relationships. Yet, James Heckman has shown that social and emotional skills yield returns exceeding narrow academic instruction. Singapore, Japan and Denmark now embed character, moral reasoning, civic education and life skills into the school day. Nepal should do the same, urgently, not as a foreign import but as a modern expression of wisdom our society has carried for centuries.

We have a young government, born of a youth movement, in a country where 40 percent are under 35. For those seeking a reform that costs little and matters enormously, here is one: Put childhood’s relational foundations at the heart of the mandate. Markets are necessary but not sufficient. They have no instinct for what children most need: presence, consistency, unhurried attention and the sense of being held by people who are not going anywhere.
